## Recommended candidates

- **10/10** — [Diversity and potential ecological roles of viruses in Pleistocene permafrost.](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-026-02685-6) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. High-priority Arctic virus metagenomics: Pleistocene Siberian permafrost vOTUs, predicted hosts, and candidate auxiliary metabolic genes.
- **10/10** — [Gelidimonas denitrificans gen. nov., sp. nov., and Gelidimonas diazotrophica sp. nov. psychrophilic bacteria involved in the nitrogen cycle in tundra soils of South Spitsbergen.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.syapm.2026.126730) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. High-priority Spitsbergen isolate-genome study describing novel psychrophilic nitrogen-cycling bacteria.
- **10/10** — [Giant viruses of the polar regions: diversity, endemism, adaptation and ecological structuring.](https://academic.oup.com/femsec/article/102/7/fiag061/8704136) — *publisher page checked; hold for full text extraction*. Current polar giant-virus review covering diversity, endemism, adaptation, and ecological structuring; valuable synthesis with overlap to existing sources.
- **10/10** — [Metagenome-assembled genomes from northern West Siberia: insights into microbial diversity in permafrost and contemporary soils.](https://doi.org/10.1093/jambio/lxag182) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. High-priority Arctic prokaryote MAG resource from dated West Siberian permafrost and contemporary soils.
- **10/10** — [Viral genetic diversity and functional potential in polar and subarctic sea ice.](https://academic.oup.com/femsec/article/102/8/fiag077/8738149) — *full text checked; promoted to curated graph*. High-priority bipolar viral metagenomics across Arctic, Baltic, and Antarctic sea ice, with host and auxiliary-gene predictions.
- **9/10** — [Dynamics of mercury contamination within the albatross and petrel community at South Georgia.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2026.128745) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. Sub-Antarctic eukaryote and geochemistry study using mercury and stable isotopes in eight seabird species at South Georgia.
- **9/10** — [Genomic adaptations of novel halotolerant bacteria from extreme North Greenland.](https://doi.org/10.1093/femsec/fiag073) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. High Arctic prokaryote culture and genomics study of novel halotolerant bacteria from northern Greenland.
- **9/10** — [In Situ Mesocosm Experiment Shows the Capability of the Microbial Community of a Canadian High Arctic Shoreline to Degrade the New Generation of Ship Fuels.](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.5c10583) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. Canadian High Arctic in situ mesocosm study of native microbial degradation of low-sulfur ship fuels.
- **9/10** — [The high Arctic resistome: stress-response genes, virulence determinants, and microbial populations in human-impacted environments of Spitsbergen.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2026.128242) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. High Arctic anthropogenic-impact metagenomics across sewage, fjord water, and glacial ice, focused on resistance and virulence genes.
- **9/10** — [Unveiling Ross Sea eukaryotic diversity through environmental DNA metabarcoding.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0141113626004289) — *full text checked; promoted to curated graph*. Two-year multi-depth Ross Sea eDNA survey directly expands Antarctic eukaryote and water-mass coverage; verified for structured curation.
- **8/10** — [Improved mapping of Arctic fractional land cover and land cover change from multi-resolution optical remote sensing.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2026.115511) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. High-priority Arctic Earth-system and terrestrial-eukaryote resource: annual 2016–2023 tundra fractional land-cover maps across three Arctic ecoregions.
- **8/10** — [Sub-Arctic bacterioplankton in-situ response to crude oil and identification of the oil-degrading community by DNA-SIP and cultivation.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marpolbul.2026.119632) — *doi abstract verified; hold for full text extraction*. Sub-Arctic in situ oil-exposure study with community profiling, DNA-SIP, and cultivation in the Faroe–Shetland Channel.

## Background-only candidates

- **6/10** — [Environmental variation structures northern peatland soil microbiome composition and function in a reindeer herding area exclosure experiment.](https://doi.org/10.1093/femsec/fiag072) — Northern boreal peatland manipulation relevant to greenhouse-gas microbiology, but the sampled fen is not clearly high-Arctic.
- **6/10** — [Genomic catalogue of giant viruses reveals expanded diversity and functional potential.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-026-02435-y) — Large global giant-virus genome catalogue is not polar-specific but is a valuable reference framework for polar Nucleocytoviricota classification and gene calling.
- **6/10** — [Trends in Aquatic Environmental DNA Research in Alaska.](https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.73925) — Review and practitioner survey of Alaska aquatic eDNA research is useful method and implementation context rather than a new primary ecological dataset.
- **5/10** — [A Roadmap for Using Hybridisation Capture-Based Target Enrichment of Ancient Environmental DNA in Palaeoecology.](https://doi.org/10.1111/1755-0998.70152) — Methodological roadmap for ancient environmental-DNA capture; useful for sedaDNA methods but not a polar evidence source itself.
- **5/10** — [Archaea-driven bioremediation of polyolefins and polyesters in extreme environments.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bidere.2026.100092) — Review of archaeal plastic-degradation evidence in extreme environments is methodologically relevant but lacks a directly polar primary dataset.
- **5/10** — [Decoding the Deep: The Ecology, Biogeography, and Evolution of Deep-Sea Viruses.](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-marine-050625-093011) — Authoritative deep-sea virus synthesis is useful context for polar deep-ocean virology but does not itself provide a polar sampling claim.
- **5/10** — [From macro to meso: Latitudinal distribution of plastic fragments from the Arctic to the tropics and influence of the environmental conditions.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marpolbul.2026.119955) — Arctic-to-tropical beach-plastic comparison supplies environmental-contaminant context but does not characterize polar microbiomes or biological processes.
- **5/10** — [Genomic characteristics and geographical distribution of uncultivated soil prokaryotes.](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-026-13092-0) — Global soil-genome analysis with an Arctic-specific hidden-diversity result, but no polar-focused sampling design.
- **4/10** — [Protracted ocean circulation slowdown drove exceptional ice-sheet melting during ice age termination IV.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73733-6) — Termination-IV circulation and ice-sheet feedback study offers paleoceanographic context but does not directly characterize the modern Arctic or Antarctic system.
- **3/10** — [The chemistry of habitable oceans in the Solar system.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74955-4) — Planetary-ocean chemistry synthesis may provide broad habitability context but lies outside the operational Arctic–Antarctic environmental graph.

## Deferred candidates

- **9/10** — [Late-summer hotspot of particulate organic matter and essential omega-3 fatty acids at the sea-ice bottom in the Central Arctic Ocean.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marenvres.2026.108308) — Direct Central Arctic bottom-ice versus under-ice POM and omega-3 comparison; highly relevant, but only the DOI abstract has been verified.
- **8/10** — [Complete genome sequence of a novel Pseudomonas sp. GW-45 isolated from Antarctic Ardley cove showing DMSP degradation capability.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.margen.2026.101262) — Ardley Cove Pseudomonas isolate grows on DMSP and carries sulfur- and nitrogen-cycle genes; DOI abstract verified, full text still required.
- **8/10** — [Mechanistic insights into diatom iron uptake: In vitro siderophore characterization and in silico modelling and docking of ISIPs in iron-limiting conditions.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marenvres.2026.108342) — Southern Ocean diatom–bacterium iron-acquisition study with experimental siderophore chemistry and modeled ISIP binding; full-text causal boundaries require extraction.
- **8/10** — [Regional contrasts in phytoplankton communities and organic carbon pools: Hydrographic forcing and zooplankton grazing in the Cosmonaut and Cooperation Seas.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marpolbul.2026.120114) — Fifty-five-station Cosmonaut and Cooperation Seas phytoplankton, hydrography, grazing, POC and DOC study; retain for full-text structured curation.
- **8/10** — [Rhodococcus dendrobeaniae sp. nov., an actinomycete isolated from an Arctic marine invertebrate exhibiting cytotoxic activity, and an emended description of Rhodococcus sovatensis.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.syapm.2026.126755) — Arctic Barents Sea isolate with genome-resolved taxonomy and biosynthetic potential; retain for full-text extraction before claim-level promotion.
- **8/10** — [Shelf-slope variability and permafrost influence shape refractory porewater dissolved organic matter across the East Siberian-Chukchi Arctic margin.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marenvres.2026.108267) — East Siberian–Chukchi porewater DOM study directly informs permafrost influence, benthic–pelagic exchange, and refractory carbon; await full-text extraction.
- **7/10** — [Epibenthic food web structure across the Northeast Greenland seascape.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marenvres.2026.108295) — Northeast Greenland epibenthic stable-isotope food-web baseline is relevant to Arctic eukaryotes and carbon sources; await full-text extraction.
- **7/10** — [Genomic analysis of an Arctic marine Tenacibaculum sp. SM2510 reveals its genetic potential for glutathione utilization.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.margen.2026.101264) — Kongsfjorden Tenacibaculum isolate genome predicts glutathione uptake, antioxidant defense, and nutrient use; claims need full-text verification.
- **7/10** — [Long-term retention of paralytic shellfish toxins in a Pacific Arctic bivalve population.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.hal.2026.103161) — Three-year southern Chukchi bivalve toxin-retention study is relevant to Arctic eukaryotes and food-web function; await full-text extraction.
- **6/10** — [Photochemical evolution of atmospheric brown carbon in Arctic Svalbard.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhazmat.2026.143086) — Year-round Svalbard brown-carbon photochemistry is relevant to the polar Earth-system layer but peripheral to the microbiome core; hold for detailed atmospheric curation.
- **4/10** — [Bioaccumulation of trace elements by Leach's storm-petrels (Hydrobates leucorhous) in the North and South Atlantic Ocean during the non-breeding period.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.marpolbul.2026.119998) — Storm-petrel trace-element and isotope study may inform mobile eukaryote exposure across Atlantic wintering regions, but explicit polar linkage is limited in the abstract.
- **4/10** — [Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in commercially important marine species of fish and shellfish from Alaska and implications for human exposure.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.toxrep.2026.102302) — Alaska seafood PFAS survey has regional eukaryote and contaminant context but is peripheral to microbial and cryosphere processes; defer pending scope expansion.
